page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a notable contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, ranks in the top 25%, indicating strong individual core execution. However, multi-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench falls into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is mixed, with small-block read-only and large-block write operations scoring in the bottom 25%, while large-block read-only bandwidth and PassMark memory scores achieve average tier rankings. Computational tasks such as software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing show weaker results, whereas text processing and single-threaded compression tasks maintain average performance.

Given its hardware profile and performance characteristics, the ecs.g7a.xlarge is suited for general-purpose workloads that require dedicated CPU resources but do not demand intensive multi-threaded scaling or high-throughput local storage. Appropriate workloads include lightweight web serving, basic text processing, and single-threaded application tasks. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable baseline performance for entry-level enterprise applications, though the lack of local storage requires external block storage integration.
